title: AI Resume Analyzer Meeting (Assignment PDF Conversation)
description: Stakeholder meeting discussing an AI-powered resume screening and candidate ranking system for software engineering roles.

utterances.speaker: Hiring Manager
utterances.text: We need to build an AI-based resume analyzer that can automatically shortlist candidates for our software engineering roles.

utterances.speaker: ML Engineer
utterances.text: Okay. How should the system decide which candidates to shortlist?

utterances.speaker: Hiring Manager
utterances.text: It should rank them based on relevance to the job description.

utterances.speaker: ML Engineer
utterances.text: How are we defining relevance?

utterances.speaker: Hiring Manager
utterances.text: Mainly skills and experience. And overall profile strength.

utterances.speaker: ML Engineer
utterances.text: What does overall profile strength include?

utterances.speaker: Hiring Manager
utterances.text: Things like good companies, solid projects, impactful work.

utterances.speaker: ML Engineer
utterances.text: Should we prioritize years of experience?

utterances.speaker: Hiring Manager
utterances.text: Yes, but not strictly. Sometimes a strong fresher is better than someone with 5 average years.

utterances.speaker: ML Engineer
utterances.text: Do we have historical hiring data to train the system?

utterances.speaker: Hiring Manager
utterances.text: We have past resumes and hiring decisions, but they're not very structured.

utterances.speaker: ML Engineer
utterances.text: How accurate should the system be?

utterances.speaker: Hiring Manager
utterances.text: It should be good enough so that HR trusts it.
ambiguousPhrases: good enough so that HR trusts it

utterances.speaker: ML Engineer
utterances.text: Do we need explainability? For example, why a candidate was ranked higher?

utterances.speaker: Hiring Manager
utterances.text: Yes, that would be useful.

utterances.speaker: ML Engineer
utterances.text: Are there any constraints regarding bias or fairness?

utterances.speaker: Hiring Manager
utterances.text: Yes, we must avoid bias, especially related to gender or college background.
ambiguousPhrases: especially related to gender or college background

utterances.speaker: ML Engineer
utterances.text: Should the system process resumes in real-time or batch mode?

utterances.speaker: Hiring Manager
utterances.text: It shouldn't be slow.

utterances.speaker: ML Engineer
utterances.text: What is the expected response time per resume?

utterances.speaker: Hiring Manager
utterances.text: Ideally quick.

utterances.speaker: ML Engineer
utterances.text: What is the timeline for delivery?

utterances.speaker: Hiring Manager
utterances.text: We need an MVP soon.

sampleClarifications.question: What is the precise latency threshold for single resume parsing and batch screening?
sampleClarifications.triggeredBy: It shouldn't be slow / Ideally quick
options: Single resume < 1.5 seconds, batch of 100 resumes < 30 seconds
Single resume < 5 seconds, batch of 500 resumes < 5 minutes
Real-time streaming parsing < 500ms per resume
sampleClarifications.selectedResponse: Single resume parsing must be under 1.5s (95th percentile) and batch upload of 100 resumes must complete within 30 seconds.

sampleClarifications.question: How should bias mitigation be enforced and measured across gender and educational background?
sampleClarifications.triggeredBy: Yes, we must avoid bias, especially related to gender or college background.
options: Pre-processing anonymization (mask name, gender, college tier) + Disparate Impact Ratio >= 0.80
Post-processing calibration across demographic bins with statistical parity
Blind screening with adversarial debiasing in embedding layer
sampleClarifications.selectedResponse: Anonymize PII and college names before scoring; enforce Disparate Impact Ratio (DIR) between 0.80 and 1.25 across gender and college tiers.

sampleClarifications.question: What quantifiable accuracy metric defines 'good enough for HR trust' for candidate shortlisting?
sampleClarifications.triggeredBy: It should be good enough so that HR trusts it.
options: Top-10 Ranking Precision >= 85% and Recall@20 >= 80% compared to senior technical recruiter consensus
F1-Score >= 0.90 across all shortlisted candidates
Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR) >= 0.75 on historical test sets
sampleClarifications.selectedResponse: Top-10 shortlisting Precision >= 85% and NDCG@10 >= 0.82 evaluated against blind human recruiter consensus.

sampleClarifications.question: What specific explainability format is required for why a candidate is ranked or disqualified?
options: SHAP/feature breakdown showing matched skills %, years of relevant experience, and key project impact badges
Textual bullet points highlighting top 3 strengths and missing prerequisite skills
Interactive match scorecard with side-by-side JD skill overlap
sampleClarifications.selectedResponse: Provide a structured breakdown for each candidate: matched required skills %, matched preferred skills %, quantified project score, and 3 bullet justifications for ranking.

sampleClarifications.question: What resume file formats, parsing schemas, and unstructured historical data cleanup methods must be supported?
sampleClarifications.triggeredBy: We have past resumes and hiring decisions, but they're not very structured.
options: Support PDF, DOCX, TXT up to 10MB; OCR fallback; semi-automated labeling pipeline for historical resumes
Only PDF support with structured JSON resume format export
Multi-lingual resume extraction with cloud OCR API
sampleClarifications.selectedResponse: Support PDF and DOCX up to 10MB; parse unstructured text into standardized JSON schema (skills, education, work history, projects); run automated data cleaning on historical logs.

sampleClarifications.question: How should 'profile strength' (good companies, solid projects) and freshers vs experienced candidates be weighted?
sampleClarifications.triggeredBy: Things like good companies, solid projects, impactful work / Sometimes a strong fresher is better than someone with 5 average years.
options: Dynamic weighted scoring: 40% Verified Project Complexity & Skills, 30% Job Relevance, 20% Impact/Achievements, 10% Years of Exp with fresher bonus
Fixed rule filter based on company tier list and minimum 3 years experience
Pure semantic embedding similarity score without separate company weighting
sampleClarifications.selectedResponse: Weighting formula: 45% Skill Match & Demonstrated Tech Stack, 35% Project Impact & Scope (open source, deployed apps), 20% Relevant Experience; allow freshers with high project scores to outrank generic profiles.

sampleClarifications.question: What is the concrete deadline and core scope for the 'MVP soon' deliverable?
options: 4-week MVP deliverable: Web dashboard, single & batch resume upload (PDF/DOCX), scoring engine, explainability breakdown, and CSV export
2-week prototype with basic keyword matching
8-week production release with ATS integration
sampleClarifications.selectedResponse: MVP delivery in 4 weeks: Web-based candidate shortlisting portal supporting PDF/DOCX ingestion, JD matching, top-N ranking with explainability cards, and fairness metrics dashboard.

title: Fintech Real-Time Fraud Prevention System
description: Requirement meeting for an instant payment fraud detection and alert engine.

utterances.speaker: Product Manager
utterances.text: We need a fraud detection system for our payment gateway to block suspicious transactions.

utterances.speaker: Architect
utterances.text: What type of latency constraints do we have for in-flight transaction authorization?

utterances.speaker: Product Manager
utterances.text: It has to be really fast so customers don't feel any lag during checkout.

utterances.speaker: Architect
utterances.text: What is our expected transaction throughput during peak sales?

utterances.speaker: Product Manager
utterances.text: Huge volume, like during Black Friday we get lots of traffic.

utterances.speaker: Compliance Lead
utterances.text: What about false positives? If we block genuine cards, customers will be angry.

utterances.speaker: Product Manager
utterances.text: False positives should be minimal, but security is number one.

sampleClarifications.question: What is the maximum allowable latency for fraud scoring during transaction authorization?
sampleClarifications.triggeredBy: really fast / don't feel any lag
options: p99 latency < 50ms
p95 latency < 100ms
Asynchronous review within 1 minute
sampleClarifications.selectedResponse: p99 scoring latency must be <= 45ms within the payment authorization pipeline.

sampleClarifications.question: What is the peak transactions per second (TPS) target for high-traffic events?
options: 15,000 TPS peak with horizontal auto-scaling
5,000 TPS peak
50,000 TPS distributed global gateway
sampleClarifications.selectedResponse: Support sustained 12,000 TPS and peak 25,000 TPS with zero message loss.

sampleClarifications.question: What is the acceptable False Positive Rate (FPR) and target Fraud Catch Rate?
options: FPR < 0.15% with Fraud Detection Rate (Recall) >= 94%
FPR < 0.5% with Recall >= 98%
sampleClarifications.selectedResponse: False Positive Rate strictly below 0.12% while maintaining fraud detection recall >= 95.5%.

title: Healthcare Clinical Decision Support & EHR Integration
description: Stakeholder discussion on AI diagnostic recommendation assistant for electronic health records.

utterances.speaker: Chief Medical Officer
utterances.text: We want an AI copilot to assist clinicians during patient diagnosis and flag drug interactions.

utterances.speaker: Lead Developer
utterances.text: How will patient data be ingested and stored?

utterances.speaker: Chief Medical Officer
utterances.text: It needs to follow all standard medical security rules and connect with our hospital system.

utterances.speaker: Lead Developer
utterances.text: What level of confidence should trigger a drug interaction warning to doctors?

utterances.speaker: Chief Medical Officer
utterances.text: Only show high risk alerts so doctors don't get alert fatigue, but don't miss anything dangerous.

sampleClarifications.question: Which specific healthcare interoperability and privacy standards must be implemented?
sampleClarifications.triggeredBy: standard medical security rules / hospital system
options: HL7 FHIR Release 4 RESTful API + HIPAA BAA compliance + AES-256 at rest & TLS 1.3 in transit
Basic DICOM and PDF export
Generic webhook integration
sampleClarifications.selectedResponse: Full HL7 FHIR v4 integration with SMART-on-FHIR authentication; HIPAA, HITECH, and SOC2 Type II compliance with end-to-end audit logging.

sampleClarifications.question: What classification threshold and severity grading defines high-risk drug interaction alerts?
sampleClarifications.triggeredBy: high risk alerts / alert fatigue / anything dangerous
options: Contraindication Class 1 (life-threatening) mandatory interruptive modal; Class 2/3 non-interruptive banner; Sensitivity >= 99.8%
Warn on all interactions
Only warn if patient has existing allergies
sampleClarifications.selectedResponse: Class 1 (severe/fatal) interactions trigger interruptive alerts with >= 99.9% sensitivity; Class 2/3 render as asynchronous sidebar notices to eliminate alert fatigue.
